title: Confidence and Uncertainty Analysis
main_findings: Correct predictions showed modestly higher model confidence and confidence margin, and lower entropy, than misclassified predictions. However, the distributions overlapped substantially.
Median model confidence was 0.7082 for correct predictions and 0.6613 for misclassified predictions. The exploratory comparison yielded p = 0.0687.
Confidence did not meaningfully track continuous end-to-end EF disagreement. Spearman rho was 0.0400 for maximum confidence, 0.0830 for confidence margin, and -0.0753 for normalized entropy.
The Intermediate-EF reference class was the most challenging subgroup, with 35.71% accuracy, compared with 81.25% for Lower-EF and 85.00% for Higher-EF.
Intermediate-EF cases also had lower median confidence and margin and higher median entropy than the Lower and Higher EF groups.
Confidently incorrect predictions were observed. The most confident misclassification had a maximum class score of 0.8882.
Therefore, classifier confidence alone is insufficient as a patient-level reliability or safety indicator in the present frozen system.
application_implication: A future assistive interface may display model confidence as supplementary information, but the present results do not justify using a confidence-only cutoff to determine whether an output is safe or reliable. Reliability review should instead consider multiple pipeline signals, such as segmentation/measurement quality, EF disagreement patterns, image quality, and classifier uncertainty.
limitations: Only 50 frozen evaluation patients were analyzed.
No independent calibration dataset was available in this phase.
The evaluation set had historical pilot exposure.
Subgroup analyses contain small sample sizes.
No operational confidence threshold was validated.
